value.why: Scoring probability and clean-sheet propensity for each team.
Lambdas determine P(score >= 1).
Joint low-score cells decide BTTS-no.
Keeper conversion adjusts clean-sheet odds.
Missing defenders/strikers shift scoring probabilities.
Team failing-to-score streaks regress.
Clean-sheet streak partly keeper luck.
Openness raises joint scoring.
First-half variant needs the split.
Leading team's defensive posture reduces late conceding.
Regulation/half definition and abandonment.
Confirmed defenders/forwards and keeper.

Shots on target for and against separate each side's shot-stopping luck and defensive volume when estimating its shutout probability (the BTTS-No channel); context to soc.gk, whose shrunk keeper effect is the main clean-sheet term.
Red-card variance alters scoring.
Set-piece route for the weaker team to score.
BTTS-No wins are blanks by one side; excess zero mass is the direct driver and is not in any existing input.
Turns static lambdas into the sequential process that BTTS actually follows.
Gives the minimum-lambda channel a quality-weighted measurement instead of a mean.

2H BTTS only (stage s6 and the conditional interaction with soc.half_level_dependence_rho): the half-time score selects the second-half rate multipliers (level keeps both rates near baseline; a one-goal lead raises the trailer's and lowers the leader's); not used for full-match or 1H series.

1H and 2H BTTS only (stage s6): both sides must score inside one 45-minute window, so the dependence between the two half-window scoring processes corrects the product (1-exp(-l_home_h))(1-exp(-l_away_h)); this is a separate parameter from the full-match Dixon-Coles rho.

Cross-division cup ties (Copa del Rey, Copa do Brasil, Coupe de France, FA Cup and DFB-Pokal early rounds, Israeli Cup), stage s1: the two sides share no league opponents, so this bridge puts the weaker side's lambda, which binds BTTS Yes, on a common scale; irrelevant within one league.

Cross-division cup ties only, stage s1: a heavily rotated favourite (7+ changes) raises the underdog's scoring chance and lowers the favourite's own clean-sheet probability, scaling the weaker side's lambda after the bridge rating.

Cup-tie BTTS (e.g. KXCOPADELREYBTTS, KXCONMEBOLSUDBTTS), stage s4: in a second leg the aggregate sets which side must score and how open the 90 minutes are, changing the goal process without changing the contract (extra time is excluded from settlement); no role in league fixtures.

Stage s4 lineup-news shock: expected rotation of starters (low-stakes league games, congested cup weeks) changes each side's scoring chance and clean-sheet probability for that fixture; context because it is only knowable partially before the lineup timestamp.

Stage s4: dead rubbers and six-pointers change a side's risk posture and so both scoring rates; the direction for BTTS is not established (open dead rubbers and cagey high-leverage games are both plausible), so it is context to be estimated, not a signed adjustment.

1H and 2H BTTS only (stage s6): per-team half-specific attack and defence rates l_h from each team's half share of goals feed the half-window product; full-match series use soc.xg_adjusted_ratings instead.

Stage s4 and the event-stream and referee/penalty required_data feeds: a penalty award (about a quarter of matches, roughly 75-80% conversion) is a near-certain scoring route for an otherwise blanked side, so referee/VAR and team penalty propensity move P(weaker side scores); also in the game_total blueprint, carried here explicitly so the archetype's own list supplies what stage s4 asserts.

value.hypothesis: Consistency between hazard integral and the 0-0 cell is a check on the goal model.
Dead-ball and penalty events provide step increments in hazard not captured by open-play xG.

The first-goal minute and route are jointly distributed: set pieces concentrate after minute 30 while penalties are timed by referee decisions, so the intensity decomposition changes the win-the-race probability and the minute distribution together.
value.how_to_test: Compute the first-goal CDF by route and compare with a pooled hazard in held-out matches.

value.hypothesis: Home advantage multiplies the intensity ratio, so in a neutral-venue final it disappears and the favourite's first-scorer odds fall by an amount to be estimated from neutral-venue finals relative to the same pairing at home.
value.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer indicator with home and neutral flags.

value.hypothesis: Only in competitions that play extra time: the no-goal leg needs 0-0 at 90 and no extra-time goal, so its price is the product of the 0-0 cell and the tired-play survival over 30 minutes; in leagues and straight-to-penalties cups the extra-time factor is exactly one.
value.how_to_test: Compare goalless-after-120 frequencies in cup ties with ET against the 0-0-at-90 cell times modelled ET survival.

value.hypothesis: A referee with a high penalty-award rate raises the penalty share of first goals for the side that wins more box entries, so the route mix and the referee propensity multiply; the effect is largest when open-play xG is close and a single penalty decides the race.
value.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer probability with a referee penalty-rate x box-entry-share term on held-out matches.

value.hypothesis: In a second leg the aggregate decides who must attack: a side leading by two sits deep and the trailing side presses from kickoff, so the first-goal hazard is shifted toward the trailing team and the no-goal mass rises when the leader is strong enough to defend; the cagey factor is a function of the aggregate state, not a constant.
value.how_to_test: Bin second-leg FTTS outcomes by aggregate margin and compare first-scorer shares and goalless rates to first-leg baselines.

value.why: Season/tournament simulation - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Leverage in fixtures near the cut.
Tiebreaks and slot allocation.
Administrative sanctions near the cut.
Group permutations and simultaneous matches.
Aggregate state and extra-time rules.
Advancement beyond 90 minutes.
Uncertainty near the cut - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Direct-rival fixtures - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Key absences late in season - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
National-team duty for tournament-style competitions.
Defines qualification and advancement wording.
Narrative-level stakes beyond leverage.
Shootout skill for knockout advancement.
Postponed fixtures change the cut-off schedule.
Late squad news in decisive matches.
Makes the qualification threshold a random variable rather than a constant, which the table simulation alone omits.
Last-place contracts are minimum order statistics and are not equal to relegation odds.
Provides the structured tree the existing inputs (aggregate state, ET model, shootout skill) only describe separately.

Prices stage-reach counts, maxima and $1/N dead heats over sets of teams (furthest-advancing confederation nation, debutant and host counts, non-top-10 semi-finalist) from the per-draw stage-reached vector; the same simulation already serves competition_winner_and_top_n.
Converts the table simulation into promotion probability for KXEFLPROMO and KXLALIGA2PROMO, whose YES includes the play-off route.

Stage s2 draws in-season dismissals for each simulated path from this hazard (winless runs, points per game below ratings-implied expectation, tenure; Cox model on top-5 league changes) for relegation-zone clubs, so P(relegated) becomes a mixture over change paths; it supplies only the timing/probability of a change, not the rating shift (that is soc.transfers).

Stage s2 and the interaction [soc.manager_dismissal_hazard, soc.transfers, soc.comp_sim]: once a simulated path draws a dismissal, remaining fixtures use the re-blended rating w(m) x (pre-change rating + d_mc) + (1 - w(m)) x rating estimated under the new manager, with w(m)=6/(6+m) and the bounce shift d_mc held at 0 until estimated (much of it is mean reversion); the same input carries window-move squad-value shifts for early-season and post-window futures. Secondary: it changes the rating of a few clubs on a subset of paths, whereas the hazard decides whether a path switches.

Stage s2: late-season rotation (dead rubbers, congested cup schedules) lowers a side's expected strength in specific remaining fixtures of the run-in, which the remaining-schedule simulation must apply per match rather than as a season average; context because the sign of the effect for cut-line clubs is not established.

Stage s4: KXUCLMOV trades the regular-time / extra-time / penalty-shootout split of an advancement, so the tie tree's branch probabilities are calibrated against realised method-of-victory frequencies; only used for the MOV series, not for plain advancement or table markets.

Stage s5: KXUCLRO16 (top 8 or win the knockout play-off) and KXUCLBOTTOM (36th place) are settled on the 36-team league-phase table over eight unbalanced fixtures, which a group-table model cannot represent; not used for domestic table series.

Stage s7: the host series (KXWCHOSTKO, KXWCHOSTSTAGE) lift each host nation's group-match strength by the home edge in its own country, applied before the joint stage-reached simulation; not needed for neutral-site or domestic table markets.

value.hypothesis: A goalkeeper strong at shot-stopping both lowers ET concessions and raises shootout win probability, so the ET and penalty MOV legs for that team are positively linked rather than independent.
value.how_to_test: Simulate MOV legs with and without a shared keeper effect and compare to historical team-level ET and shootout win records.

value.hypothesis: A side whose starters carry heavy recent minutes depends more on bench quality in extra time; unequal load plus unequal depth tilts who scores in the 91-120 window, not only whether anyone does.
value.how_to_test: In historical extra-time matches, compare ET goal share against the difference in starter minutes load across the sides, split by bench-value gap.

value.hypothesis: Hypothesis, not evidenced: a depleted favourite loses more in the 90-minute gap than in extra time if its bench is deep, because the 91-120 window depends on substitutes and fitness as much as on the starting XI; the lineup shock therefore enters the regulation node and the extra-time node with different weights.
value.how_to_test: Estimate the regulation and extra-time node probabilities with a lineup-strength interaction term on historical finals and cup ties that reached 120 minutes; keep it only if the extra-time coefficient differs from the regulation one.

value.hypothesis: In a second leg extra time is reached only when the aggregate, not the match score, is level after 90, and the side that still trails the aggregate keeps a different risk posture in the 91-120 window; the Method phase therefore depends on the aggregate state and not only on the second-leg score, moving mass between Regular Time and Extra Time legs.
value.how_to_test: Tabulate historical two-leg ties that reached extra time by first-leg margin and compare 91-120 goal rates and outcome phases with the state-conditioned prediction.

value.hypothesis: The level-at-90 probability depends on both the gap and the total rate; a cagey final lowers total goals, which raises the draw cell by more when the gap is small than when one side is a heavy favourite.
value.how_to_test: In historical finals, regress level-at-90 on gap bucket x competition goal multiplier and test the product term.

value.hypothesis: Extra-time goal intensity and its direction depend on which side keeps quality on the bench and substitutes left; a side with a strong bench raises ET decisiveness and its own ET-win share.
value.how_to_test: Among ET matches, compare ET goal share against the difference in bench value and subs remaining at 90 minutes.

value.hypothesis: Without home advantage the expected goal gap shrinks toward zero, so draw mass rises irrespective of rho; the Dixon-Coles correction then decides how much of that diagonal mass sits on 0-0 and 1-1 rather than 2-2, so the venue split moves the level probability both through the gap and through the share of low cells.
value.how_to_test: Contrast draw rates in neutral-venue finals with home/away matches at the same rating gap, with and without the rho correction, to separate the gap effect from the low-cell effect.

value.hypothesis: Heat and humidity compound the fatigue of the 91-120 window: in hot kickoffs the ET goal rate falls below the pro-rata discount and the share of level-at-120 matches rises, moving mass from Extra Time to Penalty Shootout legs.
value.how_to_test: Among extra-time matches, regress ET goals per 30 minutes on kickoff temperature/humidity with competition fixed effects.
